reviews.text: my dog looks forward to going to class!

A great place to learn with your dog. My dog has come so far thanks to the wonderful instructors. The instructors help you bring out the best in your dog while you both gain confidence, grow, and learn how to communicate with your dog. Highly recommend.

I love this club.  The instructors are very knowledgeable and friendly.  They have many years of training under their belt.  The training area is very clean and they have lots of classes throughout the week and weekend too.  Cost is excellent  for the service you get. Highly recommend!!!!!!!!!

A family member brought a Red Field Setter to our urban home. I was at a complete loss on how to live with such a high energy and curious dog. Club members were committed to helping us learn how to accommodate the needs of the breed including exercise, training and love; and, now Seamus is a law enforcement therapy dog and has several titles including Elite Performer Tricks Dog which is the highest level achievable.

I originally brought my dog  Luna to SICDTC for basic training because when I first adopted her, she had a lot of energy and we had a lot to learn together. I enjoyed the classes and saw so much progress in her that I continued enrolling in additional classes to further her training. What started as simply wanting a well-mannered dog eventually grew into something I never expected—we now compete together in Rally and Obedience, and I became a club member along the way.

SICDTC has played such an important role in how far Luna and I have come as a team. The instructors have taught me so much, and the club has given us a wonderful, supportive community of people who genuinely want to see each other succeed. I’m incredibly grateful for everything we’ve learned and for the friendships I’ve made along the way.

I have been going to Scent Work Classes at Staten Island Companion Dog Training Club with Ana Cilursu for a couple of years. I became a member of the club a year ago. Both of my dogs and I have LOVED the classes. The training experiences could not be better. I've enjoyed the camaraderie and kindness of the members. The trials are well organized and a pleasure to attend. I joined a pop up Rally Class with Sam scheduled to provide a last minute practice for members attending the Trial scheduled for the following weekend. It feels like everything is geared to helping the members do their best in their training and trialing journey. I'm so happy I joined Staten Island Companion Dog! I highly recommend the club!

I adopted my puppy in 2022 and started her training at PetSmart. As I got to know my puppy better, I decided she'd make a great Therapy Dog. While investigating HOW to become a Therapy Dog Pair, I was introduced to The Staten Island Companion Dog Training Club. This amazing group of caring and helpful (mostly volunteers) have helped both me and my dog learn how to work together. She is now a Certified Canine Good Citizen (after completing the Beginner II class) and we are now a Certified Therapy Dog Pair (after completing the Therapy Dog Training class) with The Bright and Beautiful Therapy Dogs, Inc. Since that time, I've become a member of the club and we've taken Agility For Fun. There are loads of continuous learning courses as well as competition classes if you and your dog are so inclined. They serve and understand all breeds ESPECIALLY mixed breeds and help teach owners how to manage behavior without damaging the spirit. I've learned alot and look forward to learning more. I highly recommend this club whether you just want to learn how to have a well-behaved dog or you want to train to compete.
Best decision I made with my dog!
Took my money and never alerted me for class schedule. Have left several message and sent email and have not heard back. Terrible service.

Let’s be honest. This is a pretty cute senior citizen convention but NOT the staff to train your dog. There’s not a single young trainer in the facility and the energy level of trainers provided is far from the ability to train young energetic dogs, several at the time at that, or do half the stuff that’s advertised on their website for into classes.  Training grandmas have a pretty high passive aggressive factor and make passive aggressive comments all throughout  the sessions, they never understand the question and divert the answer somewhere in a  different direction replying with what they know, rather than what was asked, rude, brief answers not only towards me but other members as well were in the air during my classes. The environment was what I would consider toxic. They also mis understand/ don’t understand a lot, which had happened to me more than once where trainer “mis understood “ what I was asking. I honestly don’t understand where their rating comes from. This is far from friendly learning environment. If you’re looking to socialize your dog and teach it basic commands this is not the place you wanna take it to. Prior to bringing my dog here we went to petsmart and the staff there is so friendly, dogs are allowed to come up to each other and play with each other if they wish, socialize, get to know the environment, this place is strictly rules and they allow no dog communication. All the commands that were taught here my dog knew before coming here so it was a waste of money for me for one, they don’t teach leash free walking upon the completion of the introduction course as  advertised. In fact I’d probably pick pet smart over this place bc in addition to just learning the commands it was paired with hand gestures that my dog could understand and still does. This place does not do that. They just give you a leaflet at first class hoping you’d teach your dog everything yourself. We’ve completed their course but to say we’re less than happy and our expectations weren’t  that high to begin with is an understatement. We literally learned NOTHING, wasted our time and money. If you really want you dog to learn something you have to hire a one on one trainer which is what we ended up doing and he was doing better in two weeks already. If you want your dog to socialize take it to shop classes and or doggy parks . This place served no benefit for us what so ever and the nasty customer service made it worse.

Our first day of class- we didn’t know what to expect. Koda Bear was a difficult student to say the least-barking, whining, tugging and jumping! With the support and patience of Janet, Desma and John.. we began to see so much growth in Koda! Koda made strides week by week. Their constant encouragement and praises as well as their sound advice and fool proof strategies has not only benefited Koda in so many ways but for our family as a whole! The dedicated instructors are true and knowledgeable experts in this field  and they care. We feel a bit more confident and validated as we work with Koda on his journey/training. Looking forward to continuing the practice as the learning never ends. We are excited for our next stop:Beginner 2!
